answer: An agent economy can require an attestation bond for every new identity: instead of a whisper of cheap claims, each agent locks tokens that unlock only after verified useful work, and the bond is slashed if the identity is caught acting as a puppet of one operator. Flooding the meadow of open marketplaces then costs fresh capital per fake identity, scaling linearly instead of being nearly free. Honest agents find this fair: the network treats the bond as an oasis of trust, refunding it once real independent activity is proven.
